findings.claim: The S17 acceptance sentence now nests a long parenthetical (the list of matched forms) and then a dangling clause ('which matches the word gentle-ai and not gentle-ai-overlay'). The clause reads as if it modifies the parenthetical or the manual-read rule, not the regex. Splitting the regex, the read-each-match rule and the match/non-match examples into separate sentences would make the check easier to apply.

evidence: I checked the new regex `(^|[^\w.-])gentle-ai([^\w/-]|$)` against the forms the entry lists. It matches the bare call, `sh -c 'gentle-ai x'`, after `&&`, `timeout` with an absolute path, and after a pipe. It does not match `gentle-ai-overlay`, `~/.gentle-ai/y` or `/opt/gentle-ai/bin/foo`.
L25 says nine sample commands were run: five matched, three were excluded, and `echo gentle-ai` still matched. That adds up to nine.
The change touches only the feature document, so I found no code regression.
